messages:
Ava: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking we should do a staggered cutover (small-slice first) instead of the big-bang service split. Reasons: safer rollbacks, easier perf signals, and smaller blast radius. Thoughts?

Liam: +1. can you sketch the slices? curious about how we map tenant size -> slice and the canary criteria.

Sofia: Suggestion: group by 90th-percentile qps and feature flags. e.g. tiny (<=50r/s), small (50-200), medium (200-1k), large (>1k). Start with tiny+small = 20% traffic for 4h, evaluate errors/latency/ops runbook, then expand. keep timeboxes.

Ava: Yup — plan is: 1) small tenants (20% traffic) 2) add medium (50%) 3) add large (30%) — with health checks at each step. Also want a hard kill-switch and automatic fallback to facade for degraded models.

Michael: Must add observability gates: request success rate drop >1% OR p50 latency +30% -> immediate rollback. Also need end-to-end tracing on sample requests so we can attribute where latency regressed.

Liam: How do we do routing? do we tag requests by tenant tier in the router and route to the new slice? will there be state migration concerns (session/KV cache)?

Sofia: Router change is minimal: add predicate by tenant-tier header. KV cache: declare a split strategy: start with cold-warm mode (read-through to old cache, write to both) for 24h, then one-way write to new cache once warmed. ops playbook to flush stale prefixes.

Ava: Example rollout config (rough):

```
rollout_policy:
  slices:
    - name: tiny_small
      traffic_pct: 20
      duration: 4h
    - name: medium
      traffic_pct: 50
      duration: 6h
    - name: large
      traffic_pct: 30
      duration: 8h
  health_gates:
    p50_latency_increase_pct: 30
    error_rate_delta_pct: 1
  fallback: route->facade
```

Liam: Nice. ops question: who owns the rollback? primary oncall (runtime) or slice owner? we should call out responsibilities otherwise finger-pointing.

Michael: Recommend: runtime oncall executes kill-switch, slice owners handle post-mortem and remediation. Also add a canary channel and a pinned checklist in runbook.

deploy-bot: Canary started for slice tiny_small at 1793331120. Traffic ramp 0% -> 20% over 5m. Monitoring probes enabled.

Sofia: For data plane compatibility, we need a compatibility shim in the adapter for 2 weeks (translate legacy session tokens). avoid breaking clients.

Ava: Action items: 1) Sofia to draft the KV warmup script + shim (ticket: ARCH-#) 2) Liam to update router predicates and config (ticket: INFRA-#) 3) Michael to update oncall playbook and tracing sampling (ticket: SRE-#). I'll own the rollout coordination.

Liam: I'll add predicates and a dry-run flag so we can validate routing rules in staging.

Michael: Will author the SLA gate doc and put it in the runbook. Also will add a metric dashboard: rollout-summary with slices, errors, p50/p95.

Ava: Cool. if there's no major pushback I'll open the merge request for the router + rollout config tomorrow and schedule the first small-slice cutover for next Tue morning (low traffic).

Sofia: Sounds good. one ask: include a list of tenants to exclude from early slices (compliance/enterprise). we'll keep those pinned to old path until final sweep.

Ava: Good call — will add exclusion list. thanks everyone. :tada:
